sections.title: SYFHome-Hub, my home server
sections.description: A NixOS box whose configuration lives in Git: the whole system rebuilds from a single file, so reinstalling it is reproducible rather than an exercise in memory. Everything is published through a Cloudflare Tunnel, without opening a single port on the router.

items.name: NixOS
items.description: Declarative operating system. The configuration lives in a repo and is applied with one command.

items.name: Cloudflare Tunnel
items.description: Publishes services to the internet with no open ports and no need for a static IP.

items.name: Nginx Proxy Manager
items.description: Reverse proxy sitting in front of every internal service.

items.name: AdGuard Home
items.description: Ad-blocking DNS and DHCP server for the whole home network.

items.name: Paperless-NGX
items.description: Document management: every piece of paper scanned, indexed and searchable.

items.name: wg-easy
items.description: WireGuard VPN with a web UI to reach the network from outside.

items.name: Docker
items.description: Services that aren't NixOS modules run in containers.

sections.title: My working setup
sections.description: A modest laptop pushed as far as it goes: no heavy desktop environment, only the window I need on screen, and nearly everything a keystroke away. None of this is for looks — it is what lets a 15 GB machine run containers, a dev server and an editor at the same time.

items.name: HP 15s
items.description: Intel Core i7-1255U with 15 GB of RAM. The machine I work on every day, at home and away.

items.name: Three screens
items.description: The laptop display plus an Acer EK321Q and an AOC 27B3HM turned to portrait, which is where documentation and logs live.

items.name: CachyOS
items.description: Arch tuned for performance. Up-to-date packages without having to assemble the system from scratch.

items.name: Hyprland
items.description: A tiling compositor on Wayland. No mouse needed to place windows: each one lands where it belongs.

items.name: kitty and fish
items.description: A GPU-accelerated terminal and a shell that completes from history without needing to be configured.

items.name: tmux
items.description: Sessions that survive closing the terminal and reconnecting over SSH to the server.

items.name: Neovim
items.description: My own configuration, no third-party distribution: LSP through Mason, formatting with conform and navigation with fzf. It shares movement keys with tmux, so jumping between pane and editor is the same gesture.

items.name: Docker
items.description: Every project with its services isolated, so the system does not fill up with dependencies nobody remembers the reason for.
